muscles.name: Biceps
muscles.description: Front of upper arm responsible for elbow flexion and forearm supination.

machines.name: Barbell Curl Station
machines.notes: Use a straight bar or EZ-bar with room in front of a mirror to monitor form.

exercises.name: Barbell Curl
steps: Stand tall with your feet about shoulder-width apart, holding the barbell with an underhand grip.
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides and your chest up.
Curl the bar upward in a smooth arc until your hands are around shoulder height.
Squeeze your biceps at the top for a brief pause.
Lower the bar under control until your arms are fully extended without locking out the elbows.
exercises.description: A classic mass-building exercise for the biceps that also engages the brachialis and forearms. You should feel most of the tension on the front of your upper arms, especially in the mid to top range of the curl.
commonMistakes: Using momentum and swinging the torso backward to lift the weight.
Letting the elbows drift forward or away from the ribcage, turning it into a shoulder exercise.
Dropping the bar too quickly instead of controlling the negative portion of the lift.
Curling the wrists instead of keeping them neutral, which stresses the joints.

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Curl
steps: Grip the EZ-bar on the angled sections with an underhand grip.
Stand upright with your shoulders back and elbows close to your sides.
Curl the bar toward your shoulders while exhaling and focusing on squeezing the biceps.
Hold briefly at the top, then lower the bar slowly back to the starting position.
exercises.description: The EZ-bar curl reduces wrist strain compared to a straight bar, making it more comfortable for many lifters while still heavily targeting the biceps.
commonMistakes: Using too narrow or too wide a grip, putting unnecessary stress on wrists and elbows.
Letting shoulders roll forward, which reduces biceps involvement.
Rushing the movement and bouncing at the bottom.

machines.name: Preacher Curl Bench
machines.notes: Preacher bench with barbell, EZ-bar or dumbbell for strict curls.

exercises.name: Preacher EZ-Bar Curl
steps: Adjust the preacher bench so your armpits rest comfortably at the top of the pad.
Grab the EZ-bar with an underhand grip and extend your arms over the pad.
Curl the bar upward by flexing the elbows, keeping your upper arms fixed on the pad.
Stop just before the bar is directly above your shoulders and squeeze the biceps.
Lower the bar under control until your arms are almost fully extended without locking out.
exercises.description: The preacher curl isolates the biceps and reduces the ability to cheat, making it excellent for focused muscle tension and a strong stretch at the bottom.
commonMistakes: Letting the elbows lift off the pad, which reduces isolation of the biceps.
Going too heavy and bouncing the weight from the bottom stretched position.
Hyperextending the elbows at the bottom, putting stress on the joint.

exercises.name: Preacher Dumbbell Curl
steps: Sit at the preacher bench holding a dumbbell in one hand.
Rest the back of your upper arm fully on the pad with your arm extended.
Curl the dumbbell up by flexing the elbow until your forearm is vertical.
Squeeze the biceps at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbell back to the start.
exercises.description: A unilateral variation that helps fix strength imbalances between arms while keeping the biceps under continuous tension.
commonMistakes: Letting the shoulder roll forward instead of keeping the chest up.
Using momentum to swing the dumbbell, especially near the bottom.
Not controlling the negative portion, which reduces muscle growth stimulus.

machines.name: Cable Station - Biceps
machines.notes: Adjustable cable column for curls with different attachments.

exercises.name: Cable Biceps Curl (Straight Bar)
steps: Attach a straight bar to the low pulley of a cable station.
Stand facing the machine, grasp the bar with an underhand grip and arms extended.
Curl the bar toward your shoulders, keeping your elbows glued to your sides.
Pause and squeeze the biceps at the top, then slowly lower the bar back down.
exercises.description: The cable curl provides constant tension on the biceps throughout the entire range of motion, making it great for a strong pump and muscle control.
commonMistakes: Leaning backward and using bodyweight to move the stack.
Letting the shoulders shrug up instead of keeping them down.
Allowing the weight stack to slam down between reps.

exercises.name: Cable Hammer Curl (Rope)
steps: Attach a rope handle to the low pulley.
Stand tall holding the rope with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Curl the rope upward while keeping your elbows at your sides.
At the top, flex the elbows fully and squeeze the biceps and forearms.
Lower under control until your arms are extended again.
exercises.description: Hammer-style cable curls hit the brachialis and brachioradialis along with the biceps, contributing to overall upper arm thickness.
commonMistakes: Letting elbows drift forward, reducing the tension on the brachialis.
Pulling the rope apart too early, which can shorten the effective range.
Using excessive momentum instead of strict, smooth curls.

muscles.name: Triceps
muscles.description: Back of upper arm responsible for elbow extension and lockout strength.

machines.name: Cable Station - Triceps
machines.notes: High pulley station with bar or rope attachments for extension movements.

exercises.name: Rope Pushdown
steps: Attach a rope handle to the high pulley and stand facing the cable stack.
Grip the rope with both hands and bring elbows close to your sides.
Start with your forearms up, around chest level, keeping your shoulders relaxed.
Push the rope down by extending your elbows until your arms are straight.
At the bottom, spread the rope ends slightly and squeeze your triceps.
Slowly return to the starting position while keeping your elbows fixed.
exercises.description: Rope pushdowns are a staple triceps isolation exercise, emphasizing the lateral head and giving a strong contraction at the bottom of the movement.
commonMistakes: Allowing the elbows to drift forward, turning the movement into more of a chest/shoulder exercise.
Leaning excessively over the weight and using bodyweight to push it down.
Only moving through half the range of motion and skipping full lockout or controlled negatives.
Letting the shoulders shrug up toward the ears.

exercises.name: Straight Bar Pushdown
steps: Attach a straight or angled bar to the high pulley.
Stand close to the cable machine with a slight forward lean and elbows pinned to your sides.
Extend the elbows to push the bar down until your arms are fully straight.
Briefly pause at the bottom, focusing on the triceps squeeze.
Return the bar slowly to the starting position without letting elbows move.
exercises.description: A classic triceps isolation move that allows heavier loading than many other triceps exercises. Great for building size and lockout strength.
commonMistakes: Using too much weight and letting the shoulders roll forward.
Turning it into a pullover by allowing elbows to shift forward.
Locking the elbows aggressively with a snap rather than controlled extension.

exercises.name: Overhead Cable Triceps Extension
steps: Attach a rope handle to the low pulley and stand facing away from the machine.
Hold the rope behind your head with elbows pointing forward and upper arms close to your head.
Extend your elbows to bring your hands upward until your arms are nearly straight.
Control the rope back down behind your head, feeling a stretch in the long head of the triceps.
exercises.description: Targets the long head of the triceps by putting it in a stretched, overhead position. Great for adding mass to the back of the arm.
commonMistakes: Letting the elbows flare wide instead of keeping them close to the head.
Overarching the lower back due to poor core engagement.
Using too much weight and turning the movement into a shoulder press.

machines.name: Triceps Extension Machine
machines.notes: Seated selectorized machine for elbow extension with guided path.

exercises.name: Machine Triceps Extension
steps: Adjust the seat so your elbows line up with the machine's axis of rotation.
Grip the handles with your elbows bent and tucked close to your body.
Extend your elbows to push the handles away until your arms are straight.
Pause and squeeze your triceps, then slowly return to the starting position.
exercises.description: The machine triceps extension provides a stable, guided movement that isolates the triceps without requiring much balance or technique.
commonMistakes: Setting the seat too high or too low, misaligning the elbow joint with the pivot point.
Using momentum by bouncing at the bottom of the range.
Locking out too aggressively instead of maintaining control.

machines.name: Dip Station
machines.notes: Parallel bars or dip handles for bodyweight dips; some gyms also have an assisted dip machine.

exercises.name: Bench Dip
steps: Sit on the edge of a bench and place your hands beside your hips.
Walk your feet forward and slide your hips off the bench, supporting yourself with your arms.
Lower your body by bending the elbows until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor.
Push through your palms to extend your elbows and return to the top.
exercises.description: Bench dips are an accessible way to train the triceps with bodyweight, especially for beginners or when no machines are available.
commonMistakes: Letting the shoulders roll forward, which stresses the shoulder joint.
Dropping too low, placing excessive strain on the front of the shoulders.
Keeping the feet too close, which can reduce the effective range of motion.

exercises.name: Parallel Bar Dip (Triceps Focus)
steps: Hold onto parallel bars and support your body with arms straight and legs hanging.
Keep your torso more upright and your elbows close to your sides.
Lower your body by bending the elbows until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Push yourself back up by extending the elbows to return to the top position.
exercises.description: Dips are a powerful compound exercise that heavily load the triceps while also engaging the chest and shoulders. Keeping the torso more upright shifts emphasis towards the triceps.
commonMistakes: Leaning too far forward, turning the movement into a chest dip.
Only using a short range of motion instead of going deep enough.
Allowing the shoulders to shrug excessively up toward the ears.

muscles.name: Forearms
muscles.description: Muscles of the forearm responsible for wrist flexion, extension, grip strength and forearm rotation.

machines.name: Barbell Wrist Station
machines.notes: Use a barbell and bench or your thighs as support for wrist curls and extensions.

exercises.name: Barbell Wrist Curl
steps: Sit on a bench and rest your forearms on your thighs or a flat surface, palms facing up.
Hold a barbell in your hands with wrists hanging just beyond the edge.
Curl the barbell upward by flexing your wrists as high as comfortably possible.
Pause and squeeze the forearm flexors at the top, then slowly lower the bar back down.
exercises.description: Barbell wrist curls isolate the forearm flexors and help improve grip and forearm size.
commonMistakes: Using a weight that is too heavy and relying on momentum instead of controlled movement.
Lifting the forearms off the bench or thighs instead of keeping them planted.
Not using full range of motion, cutting off the stretch at the bottom.

exercises.name: Barbell Reverse Wrist Curl
steps: Sit and rest your forearms on a bench or thighs with palms facing down.
Hold the barbell with an overhand grip, wrists hanging off the edge.
Extend your wrists upward, lifting the back of your hands toward the ceiling.
Lower the bar under control back to the starting position.
exercises.description: Reverse wrist curls target the forearm extensors on the top side of the forearm, balancing development and supporting wrist health.
commonMistakes: Using too much weight and jerking the bar up.
Allowing forearms to lift off the support surface.
Cutting the range of motion short on the way down.

machines.name: Dumbbell Forearm Station
machines.notes: Use a bench, thighs or any support with dumbbells for one-arm wrist work.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Wrist Curl
steps: Sit and hold a dumbbell in one hand with your forearm resting on a bench or your thigh, palm facing up.
Allow the wrist to extend so the dumbbell lowers toward the floor.
Curl the dumbbell upward by flexing your wrist.
Squeeze at the top, then repeat and switch arms.
exercises.description: The dumbbell wrist curl allows you to train each forearm individually, helping fix strength imbalances and improving grip strength.
commonMistakes: Using the shoulder or elbow to move the weight instead of isolating the wrist.
Moving too fast and bouncing at the bottom.
Neglecting the non-dominant side, leading to imbalances.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Reverse Wrist Curl
steps: Sit and hold a dumbbell with your palm facing down, forearm supported on a bench or thigh.
Let the wrist slowly drop down, then extend it upward lifting the back of your hand.
Focus on controlling the dumbbell throughout the movement.
Repeat for reps, then switch arms.
exercises.description: Reverse dumbbell wrist curls build the often-neglected forearm extensors, helping to balance the forearm and support healthy wrist joints.
commonMistakes: Using too heavy a dumbbell and jerking the wrist into extension.
Letting the forearm roll or rotate rather than moving only at the wrist.
Not fully lowering into the stretch at the bottom.

machines.name: Grip Trainer / Farmer's Walk
machines.notes: Implements like hand grippers, thick bars and heavy dumbbells for loaded carries.

exercises.name: Farmer's Walk
steps: Pick up a heavy dumbbell or farmer's handle in each hand.
Stand tall with your shoulders back and core braced.
Walk for a set distance or time while maintaining a strong, upright posture.
Set the weights down safely at the end of the walk.
exercises.description: Farmer's walks are one of the best functional exercises for overall grip strength, forearm development and total-body stability.
commonMistakes: Letting the shoulders slump forward instead of keeping the chest up.
Walking with short, choppy steps instead of controlled strides.
Allowing the weights to bang into the legs during the walk.

exercises.name: Hand Gripper Squeezes
steps: Hold a hand gripper in one hand with the handle seated in your palm.
Squeeze the handles together as far as you can, then slowly release.
Perform controlled repetitions or long holds, then switch hands.
exercises.description: Hand grippers are a simple and effective tool to directly strengthen your crushing grip and forearm flexors.
commonMistakes: Using only the fingertips instead of seating the handle deep in the palm.
Snapping the gripper open and closed without control.
Overtraining grip every day without rest, which can cause elbow or wrist irritation.

muscles.name: Upper Chest
muscles.description: Clavicular head of the pectoralis major responsible for upward and inward pressing angles.

machines.name: Incline Bench Press (Barbell)
machines.notes: Bench set to 30°–45° for optimal upper chest activation.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Press
steps: Lie on a 30°–45° incline bench holding a barbell with a slightly wider than shoulder-width grip.
Lower the bar in a straight line toward the upper chest/clavicle region.
Keep elbows at about 45° from the body.
Press the bar upward while squeezing the upper chest.
Lock out smoothly without overextending your shoulders.
exercises.description: One of the most effective mass builders for the upper chest. The incline angle shifts load to the clavicular head of the pecs.
commonMistakes: Setting the incline too high, turning it into a shoulder exercise.
Bouncing the bar off the chest.
Arching the lower back too aggressively.

machines.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
machines.notes: Allows a deeper stretch and greater stabilization demands.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
steps: Sit on an incline bench holding dumbbells at chest height.
Press the dumbbells upward in an arc, bringing them closer together at the top.
Lower slowly until elbows drop slightly below chest level.
Keep wrists neutral and elbows at 45°.
exercises.description: Provides a deeper stretch and better isolation of the upper chest compared to barbell versions.
commonMistakes: Pressing with elbows too flared out.
Letting the dumbbells drift too far outward.

machines.name: Incline Cable Fly Station
machines.notes: Cables allow continuous tension throughout the fly path.

exercises.name: Incline Cable Fly
steps: Attach handles to low pulleys and lie back on an incline bench.
Lift arms in a wide arc, bringing hands together above the upper chest.
Lower arms until you feel a deep pec stretch.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows to protect the joint.
exercises.description: Highly effective for isolating and shaping the upper chest with constant tension.
commonMistakes: Turning the fly into a press by bending elbows too much.
Using too much weight and losing control.
Letting shoulders roll forward at the bottom.

muscles.name: Middle Chest
muscles.description: The sternal head of the pecs responsible for horizontal pressing and fly movements.

machines.name: Flat Barbell Press
machines.notes: The king of chest mass builders.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
steps: Lie on a flat bench with your feet planted.
Hold the bar slightly wider than shoulder width.
Lower the bar to mid-chest level under control.
Press the bar upward until elbows are extended.
exercises.description: A foundational strength and hypertrophy movement that heavily loads the mid-pec fibers.
commonMistakes: Flaring elbows too wide causing shoulder stress.
Lowering bar too high toward neck.

exercises.name: Flat Dumbbell Press
steps: Lie on a flat bench with dumbbells resting on shoulders.
Press dumbbells upward in an arc toward the center.
Lower them until elbows are slightly below the bench.
Maintain a neutral wrist position.
exercises.description: Provides greater range of motion and stretch than barbell pressing.
commonMistakes: Letting dumbbells drift too far apart.

machines.name: Seated Chest Fly Machine
machines.notes: Great isolation with fixed motion path.

exercises.name: Machine Chest Fly
steps: Sit upright with chest up and shoulder blades retracted.
Hold the machine handles with elbows slightly bent.
Bring handles together in front of your chest.
Return in a slow, wide arc for a full stretch.
exercises.description: One of the best machines for isolating the mid-pecs with minimal shoulder involvement.
commonMistakes: Turning the fly into a press with too much elbow bend.
Not using full range of motion.

muscles.name: Lower Chest
muscles.description: Abdominal head of the pecs emphasized through downward pressing angles.

exercises.name: Decline Bench Press
steps: Lie on a decline bench with feet secured.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width.
Lower bar toward lower chest/upper stomach.
Press upward in a controlled arc.
exercises.description: Optimizes activation of the lower pec fibers and reduces shoulder strain.

exercises.name: Decline Dumbbell Press
steps: Lie on a decline bench with dumbbells at chest height.
Press upward bringing dumbbells slightly together at the top.
Lower slowly toward lower chest line.
exercises.description: Provides more stretch and independent arm movement than barbell pressing.
commonMistakes: Letting dumbbells drift too far sideways.
Using too high of a decline angle.

exercises.name: Cable High to Low Fly
steps: Set pulleys at the highest position.
Step forward with handles in hand, slight lean.
Bring arms downward in an arc to hip level.
Return upward under control.
exercises.description: Emphasizes the downward fiber direction of the lower chest.
commonMistakes: Using too much weight and jerking the arms down.

muscles.name: Front Delts
muscles.description: Anterior head of the deltoids responsible for forward arm lifting and pushing movements.

machines.name: Barbell Overhead Press Station
machines.notes: Standing or seated overhead press using a barbell.

exercises.name: Barbell Overhead Press (OHP)
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding the barbell at shoulder height.
Brace your core and keep your glutes tight.
Press the bar straight upward until your arms are extended.
Lower the bar slowly back to the top of your chest.
exercises.description: The foundation of shoulder strength training. Strong emphasis on front delts but also engages entire shoulder complex.
commonMistakes: Not keeping the bar path straight.

machines.name: Smith Machine Shoulder Press
machines.notes: Guided vertical path helps isolate deltoids.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Shoulder Press
steps: Sit or stand under the Smith bar with hands slightly wider than shoulders.
Unrack and lower bar to chin level.
Press upward in a straight line.
Lower under control.
exercises.description: Great for isolating the deltoids without worrying about stabilizing the bar.
commonMistakes: Using a bench angle that shifts load to upper chest.
Moving elbows too far forward or backward.

machines.name: Front Raise Dumbbell Station
machines.notes: Dumbbells for unilateral or bilateral front raises.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Front Raise
steps: Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs with palms facing down.
Raise arms straight in front until shoulder height.
Pause briefly, lower slowly.
exercises.description: Isolates the anterior deltoids with minimal involvement of other muscles.
commonMistakes: Shrugging shoulders upward during the raise.

muscles.name: Side Delts
muscles.description: Lateral head of the deltoids responsible for arm abduction and width.

exercises.name: Machine Lateral Raise
steps: Sit with pads against your elbows.
Raise arms outward to shoulder level.
Lower slowly for full stretch.
exercises.description: Provides constant tension on side delts with minimal cheating.
commonMistakes: Using too much weight and swinging.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
steps: Hold dumbbells at your sides.
Raise arms outward until they reach shoulder height.
Lower back under control.
exercises.description: A classic movement for building shoulder width and roundness.

machines.name: Cable Lateral Raise
machines.notes: Low pulley cable for unilateral side delt training.

exercises.name: Single Arm Cable Lateral Raise
steps: Attach a single handle to low pulley.
Stand sideways and grip the handle with outside arm.
Raise arm outward to shoulder height.
Lower slowly with control.
exercises.description: Provides constant tension and helps fix imbalances in shoulder strength.
commonMistakes: Leaning body excessively away from cable.
Using hips to swing the weight.

muscles.name: Rear Delts
muscles.description: Posterior head of the deltoids responsible for horizontal abduction and external rotation.

machines.name: Reverse Fly Machine (Pec Deck Rear Mode)

exercises.name: Machine Reverse Fly
steps: Sit facing the machine with chest against pad.
Hold handles with arms slightly bent.
Pull arms outward and backward in an arc.
Return forward under control.
exercises.description: Excellent isolation of the posterior deltoids with minimal trap involvement.
commonMistakes: Using upper traps to initiate movement.

exercises.name: Bent-Over Reverse Dumbbell Fly
steps: Bend forward at hips with slight knee bend.
Hold dumbbells beneath chest.
Raise arms outward and backward until shoulder height.
Lower under control.
exercises.description: A staple movement to round out shoulder development by isolating rear delts.

machines.name: Cable Face Pull Station
machines.notes: Rope + high pulley for face pulls.

exercises.name: Cable Face Pull
steps: Attach rope to high pulley.
Pull rope towards forehead with elbows flared.
Externally rotate shoulders at the end (rope splits).
Return slowly.
exercises.description: One of the best exercises for rear delts, shoulder health, posture and rotator cuff strength.
commonMistakes: Pulling with biceps instead of rear delts.
Not externally rotating at the top.

muscles.name: Lats
muscles.description: Large V-shaped back muscle responsible for pulling the arms downward and backward, creating the 'V-taper'.

machines.name: Lat Pulldown Machine
machines.notes: Primary machine for vertical pulling.

exercises.name: Wide Grip Lat Pulldown
steps: Sit down with thighs secured under pads.
Grip the bar wider than shoulder width.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest while leaning slightly back.
Squeeze your back, then return slowly to the top.
exercises.description: Classic movement for building back width and emphasizing upper lat fibers.
commonMistakes: Using momentum instead of back muscles.
Not reaching full stretch at the top.

exercises.name: Close Grip Lat Pulldown (V-bar)
steps: Attach a V-bar handle to the pulldown machine.
Sit upright and pull the handle toward your chest.
Keep elbows close to your sides.
Slowly return to full extension with stretch.
exercises.description: Better for lower lats activation and gives a deep contraction.
commonMistakes: Pulling with arms instead of lats.

machines.name: Seated Row Machine
machines.notes: Horizontal row variations for mid-back and lats.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row (Close Grip)
steps: Sit on the row bench with feet on the platform.
Grab the V-handle and sit upright.
Pull the handle into your lower stomach.
Squeeze shoulder blades together.
exercises.description: Great for thickness and mid-back development, hitting the lats and rhomboids.

exercises.name: Wide Grip Seated Row
steps: Use a wide straight bar on the row machine.
Pull the bar towards your upper stomach/lower chest.
Lean slightly forward at the stretch, then pull back upright.
exercises.description: Emphasizes rear delts, upper back, and outer lat fibers.
commonMistakes: Pulling bar too high toward neck.

machines.name: T-Bar Row Machine
machines.notes: Heavy back thickness movement.

exercises.name: T-Bar Row (Wide Grip)
steps: Stand on the platform and grip the wide handles.
Keep chest supported on pad if machine has one.
Pull handles toward your chest.
Squeeze shoulder blades, then lower slowly.
exercises.description: Thickens the entire upper/middle back and hits rear delts hard.
commonMistakes: Using too much weight and short range of motion.

exercises.name: T-Bar Row (Close Grip)
steps: Grip close neutral handles.
Pull elbows tight to your torso.
Row toward lower chest/upper stomach.
Lower with slow control.
exercises.description: Places more emphasis on lower lats and mid-back.
commonMistakes: Jerking the weight from the bottom.

muscles.name: Upper Back
muscles.description: Rhomboids, middle traps, rear delts and associated scapular retraction muscles.

machines.name: Chest Supported Row Machine
machines.notes: Great for strict form and removing lower back momentum.

exercises.name: Machine Chest Supported Row
steps: Sit with chest against the pad.
Grab handles (neutral or pronated).
Pull elbows backward while squeezing shoulder blades.
Lower under control.
exercises.description: Eliminates cheating and isolates mid/upper back perfectly.

machines.name: Reverse Grip Row (Machine)
machines.notes: Supinated grip increases biceps and lower trap contribution.

exercises.name: Machine Reverse Grip Row
steps: Use an underhand grip on machine handles.
Pull elbows tightly toward your sides.
Squeeze shoulder blades hard.
Return slowly.
exercises.description: Targets rhomboids and traps while also increasing biceps involvement.

muscles.name: Lower Back
muscles.description: Erector spinae group responsible for spinal stability, extension and posture.

machines.name: Back Extension Bench (Hyperextension)
machines.notes: 45-degree or flat hyperextension bench for lower back training.

exercises.name: Back Extensions
steps: Position hips on pad with ankles locked.
Lower torso until spine is neutral.
Extend torso upward by contracting lower back.
Avoid hyperextending at top.
exercises.description: Strengthens erectors, glutes and hamstrings for total posterior chain stability.
commonMistakes: Hyperextending the spine at the top.
Using momentum instead of controlled movement.

machines.name: Reverse Hyperextension Machine
machines.notes: Louie Simmons' legendary back rehab + strength machine.

exercises.name: Reverse Hyperextension
steps: Lie face down on the reverse hyper pad.
Hook ankles into strap or foot roller.
Lift legs upward using glutes and erectors.
Lower under control.
exercises.description: One of the safest ways to train lower back while providing decompression at the bottom.

muscles.name: Trapezius
muscles.description: Upper, middle, and lower trap muscles responsible for shrugging, scapular elevation, retraction and stabilization.

machines.name: Smith Machine Shrug Station
machines.notes: Guided vertical bar path for heavy shrugs.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Shrugs
steps: Stand upright holding Smith bar at your sides.
Shrug shoulders straight upward.
Pause and squeeze traps.
Lower slowly.
exercises.description: Allows heavy trap loading without balance limitations.

machines.name: Dumbbell Shrug Station
machines.notes: Basic free-weight trap builder.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shrugs
steps: Stand tall holding dumbbells at sides.
Shrug shoulders upward in a straight line.
Pause, squeeze traps, lower slowly.
exercises.description: Simple and highly effective trapezius developer.
commonMistakes: Using too heavy weights leading to poor form.

machines.name: Barbell Shrug Station
machines.notes: Heavy free-weight shrug options.

exercises.name: Barbell Shrug
steps: Stand holding barbell slightly in front of thighs.
Shrug upward toward ears.
Lower under control.
exercises.description: Allows maximal overload for trap development.
commonMistakes: Using too much weight and short ROM.

muscles.name: Quads
muscles.description: Muscles at the front of the thigh responsible for knee extension and powerful lower-body movements.

machines.name: Leg Press Machine
machines.notes: Heavy machine for quad-dominant leg pressing movements.

exercises.name: Leg Press
steps: Sit in the machine with feet shoulder-width apart on the platform.
Lower the sled until knees reach 90 degrees.
Press through heels to extend legs.
Avoid locking out knees at the top.
exercises.description: A safe and effective quad mass builder with controlled movement and reduced back strain.
commonMistakes: Using too short a range of motion.

machines.name: Leg Extension Machine
machines.notes: Isolation machine strictly for quadriceps.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
steps: Sit on the machine and place legs under the pad.
Extend legs by contracting quads.
Squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly with control.
exercises.description: Perfect for isolating the quadriceps, especially the rectus femoris and vastus muscles.
commonMistakes: Using momentum instead of muscle control.

machines.name: Smith Machine Squat
machines.notes: Guided squat path useful for beginners or isolation training.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Squat
steps: Stand under bar with feet slightly in front of bar path.
Lower into squat until thighs reach parallel.
Push through heels to stand back up.
exercises.description: Smith squats emphasize quads by allowing a more upright torso.
commonMistakes: Using too much weight and shallow depth.

machines.name: Barbell Squat Rack
machines.notes: The ultimate quad-building free weight exercise.

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
steps: Place bar on traps and stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Sit backward and downward into a deep squat.
Drive upward through mid-foot.
exercises.description: The king of leg exercises, heavily recruiting the quads and glutes.

muscles.name: Hamstrings
muscles.description: Posterior thigh muscles responsible for knee flexion and hip extension.

machines.name: Lying Leg Curl Machine
machines.notes: Isolates hamstring curl movement.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
steps: Lie face down and secure ankles under pad.
Curl feet toward glutes.
Lower pad under control without dropping it.
exercises.description: Isolates hamstrings effectively without loading the spine.

machines.name: Seated Leg Curl Machine
machines.notes: Safer and often more comfortable than lying curl.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
steps: Sit with legs extended under top pad.
Curl pad downward by flexing knees.
Return slowly to stretch position.
exercises.description: Great for full contraction and stretch of the hamstrings.

machines.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
machines.notes: The best free weight exercise for hamstring lengthening and hip hinge strength.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
steps: Stand with barbell at hip height.
Push hips backward while keeping bar close to legs.
Lower until hamstrings stretch strongly.
Stand back up by driving hips forward.
exercises.description: Builds strong hamstrings and glutes while teaching proper hip hinging.
commonMistakes: Bending knees too much (turns into squat).
Letting bar drift away from legs.

muscles.name: Glutes
muscles.description: Largest muscle group in the body responsible for hip thrusting, hip extension, rotation and locking out heavy lifts.

machines.name: Hip Thrust Machine
machines.notes: Popular glute-focused machine with hip thrust motion.

exercises.name: Machine Hip Thrust
steps: Sit under the padded bar and place upper back against bench.
Press hips upward by squeezing glutes.
Lower slowly with tension.
exercises.description: One of the best mass-building glute exercises with excellent isolation.
commonMistakes: Pushing through toes instead of heels.

machines.name: Barbell Hip Thrust Station
machines.notes: Most powerful free-weight glute builder.

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
steps: Sit with upper back on bench and barbell over hips.
Drive hips upward while squeezing glutes.
Pause at top.
Lower slowly.
exercises.description: The most famous glute-building exercise with maximal contraction.
commonMistakes: Using lower back to lift weight.
Letting feet be too far forward.

machines.name: Cable Glute Kickback
machines.notes: Single-leg glute focus with ankle strap.

exercises.name: Cable Glute Kickback
steps: Attach ankle strap to low pulley.
Kick leg backward in controlled arc.
Squeeze glute at top.
Return slowly.
exercises.description: Great for isolating gluteus maximus and building shape.

muscles.name: Calves
muscles.description: Gastrocnemius and soleus muscles responsible for ankle extension and lower-leg aesthetics.

machines.name: Seated Calf Raise Machine
machines.notes: Targets the soleus muscle.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
steps: Sit with knees under pad and feet on platform.
Raise heels as high as possible.
Pause at peak contraction.
Lower back to deep stretch.
exercises.description: Soleus-focused movement for deeper calf development.
commonMistakes: Using too much weight and bouncing.

machines.name: Standing Calf Raise Machine
machines.notes: Primarily targets gastrocnemius.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
steps: Stand with shoulders under pads and feet on platform.
Raise heels to full extension.
Lower slowly into deep stretch.
exercises.description: Develops the gastrocnemius for fuller upper calf shape.

machines.name: Calf Press on Leg Press Machine
machines.notes: Allows heavy loading safely.

exercises.name: Leg Press Calf Raise
steps: Place feet on bottom of leg press platform.
Push through balls of feet to raise heels.
Lower back down to full stretch.
exercises.description: Allows stronger lifters to load calves significantly.

muscles.name: Upper Abs
muscles.description: Upper fibers of the rectus abdominis, responsible for spinal flexion bringing the ribcage toward the pelvis.

machines.name: Cable Crunch Station
machines.notes: Allows weighted spinal flexion to target upper abs heavily.

exercises.name: Kneeling Cable Crunch
steps: Attach a rope to a high pulley.
Kneel facing the machine and hold rope near your ears.
Crunch forward by bringing elbows toward thighs.
Return to starting position with control.
exercises.description: One of the best weighted exercises for building thick, strong upper abs.
commonMistakes: Pulling with arms instead of abs.
Bending at hips instead of curling spine.
Using too much weight and short range of motion.

machines.name: Ab Crunch Machine
machines.notes: Selectorized machine for isolated crunch motion.

exercises.name: Machine Ab Crunch
steps: Sit with chest pad against torso.
Flex spine to bring chest pad down.
Return slowly to starting position.
exercises.description: Helps beginners feel abdominal contraction without worrying about form.
commonMistakes: Using hip flexors instead of abs.

machines.name: Decline Crunch Bench
machines.notes: Decline bench increases resistance through gravity.

exercises.name: Decline Crunch
steps: Lie on decline bench with feet locked.
Curl torso upward toward knees.
Lower under control to full stretch.
exercises.description: Harder than flat crunches due to increased resistance.
commonMistakes: Using neck muscles to pull head.

muscles.name: Lower Abs
muscles.description: Lower portion of rectus abdominis responsible for lifting pelvis toward ribcage.

machines.name: Roman Chair / Captain's Chair
machines.notes: Supports forearms while performing leg raises.

exercises.name: Captain’s Chair Leg Raise
steps: Support yourself on the arm pads.
Lift knees upward to chest level.
Lower legs slowly without swinging.
exercises.description: A powerful lower-ab contraction exercise with minimal grip involvement.
commonMistakes: Not rounding spine to engage abs.

machines.name: Hanging Leg Raise Bar
machines.notes: Advanced lower-ab exercise requiring strong core control.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
steps: Hang from pull-up bar with straight arms.
Lift legs upward while curling pelvis.
Lower legs slowly under full control.
exercises.description: One of the hardest lower ab exercises, building strength and core stability.

machines.name: Reverse Crunch on Mat
machines.notes: Floor-based lower ab contraction.

exercises.name: Reverse Crunch
steps: Lie on back with legs raised.
Curl pelvis upward to lift hips.
Lower slowly with control.
exercises.description: Perfect beginner lower-ab activation exercise.

muscles.name: Obliques
muscles.description: Twisting, side bending, and rotation muscles on the sides of the torso.

machines.name: Cable Woodchopper Station
machines.notes: High-to-low and low-to-high torso rotation.

exercises.name: Cable Woodchopper (High to Low)
steps: Attach handle high on cable stack.
Pull handle diagonally downward across body.
Twist through torso while keeping arms slightly bent.
exercises.description: Targets internal and external obliques through rotational movement.

exercises.name: Cable Woodchopper (Low to High)
steps: Attach handle low.
Pull diagonally upward across body.
Rotate torso fully.
exercises.description: Challenges obliques through upward rotational movement.

machines.name: Dumbbell Side Bend Station
machines.notes: Simple but effective oblique exercise.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Side Bend
steps: Hold dumbbell in one hand.
Lean sideways while keeping torso straight.
Contract oblique to return upright.
exercises.description: Simple unilateral oblique exercise improving symmetry and side strength.
commonMistakes: Using heavy weights and poor control.

muscles.name: Deep Core / Stability
muscles.description: Transverse abdominis, pelvic stabilizers, diaphragm and lower back stabilizing muscles.

machines.name: Plank Mat Station
machines.notes: Floor mat for planks and core stability.

exercises.name: Plank Hold
steps: Place forearms on ground.
Lift torso into straight line.
Hold position while bracing core.
exercises.description: Strengthens deep core stabilizers without spine movement.

machines.name: Ab Wheel Roller
machines.notes: Advanced anti-extension exercise.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
steps: Kneel and hold ab wheel handles.
Roll forward while keeping spine neutral.
Pull back using core contraction.
exercises.description: One of the hardest core stability exercises, requiring strong anti-extension strength.

machines.name: Stability Ball Station
machines.notes: Great tool for dynamic core movements.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Crunch
steps: Sit on ball and walk feet forward until lower back rests on ball.
Crunch torso upward.
Lower into a deep stretch.
exercises.description: Allows greater spinal range of motion for enhanced ab activation.
